paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: everything starts with God. Before there was light, before there was a sky, before there was a single baker, "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth" (Genesis 1:1). He didn't need a pile of supplies or a long to-do list. He spoke, and it was so (Genesis 1:3; Genesis 1:9). I can't even get my timer to listen to me, and He told the whole sea where to go!

And look at how He looked at it all. Again and again, "God saw that it was good" (Genesis 1:10; Genesis 1:12; Genesis 1:18; Genesis 1:21; Genesis 1:25). Then He looked at everything together, and it was "very good" (Genesis 1:31). The people were the only ones made "in His own image" (Genesis 1:27), and He blessed them and gave them work to do (Genesis 1:28). So you aren't an accident, friend. You were part of a world God Himself called very good.

Then comes the quiet part. "By the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work" (Genesis 2:2), and He blessed that day and made it holy (Genesis 2:3). Good work and good rest both come from God. So if you've been running on empty, take a breath, because the One who made everything is not in a hurry. And keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't over.
